User is planning a dinner party and enjoys experimenting with jerk seasoning, especially on chicken. Appetizers: grilled pineapple and prosciutto skewers and spicy shrimp ceviche. Main: grilled jerk chicken with mango salsa, served with roasted sweet potatoes instead of quinoa/asparagus. Season sweet potatoes with olive oil, salt, pepper, aromatics, and citrus; their sweetness balances jerk heat. Dessert: coconut-lime panna cotta topped with dessert-friendly mango salsa. For salsa, use a sweeter, fruit-forward, tangier, less-spicy version of the savory salsa: more ripe mango, reduced/omitted jalapeño, balanced lime, optional honey/agave, and mint/basil/cilantro. Suggested mix: 2 diced ripe mangos, 1/2 diced red onion, 1/4 cup cilantro, 2 tbsp lime juice, optional 1 tbsp honey/agave, salt, optional Grand Marnier. User likes creamy desserts with a tangy, refreshing contrast.

User has a cocktail-making class on Fridays and is excited to experiment with new recipes. They chose Avion Silver as their favorite tequila for homemade margaritas. They are enthusiastic about a Watermelon Basil Margarita and plan to roast the watermelon for added sweetness. Basic puree idea: blend 3–4 cups seedless watermelon, strain, then add optional sugar and lime; refrigerate briefly. Suggested drink ratio: 2 oz Avion Silver, 1 oz lime, 1/2 oz roasted-watermelon puree, 1/2 oz agave, 1/4 oz basil syrup, salt rim, ice; garnish with basil and watermelon. Basil syrup: equal parts water/sugar, steep fresh basil, strain; refrigerate up to about 2 weeks.

For class, user plans to make a Paloma and a Tequila Sour. They want to experiment with grapefruit juice, including pink or ruby varieties, and are interested in the Tequila Sour’s silky egg-white texture. Potential Tequila Sour enhancement: citrus- or spice-infused simple syrup. User appreciates practical flavor-balancing advice and experimenting with ingredients, ratios, and techniques.
